cases.title: HTML/script bytes named innocent.pdf and declared application/pdf are REJECTED
cases.steps: POST /api/documents, part filename="innocent.pdf", Content-Type: application/pdf, body = <html><script>fetch(/api/customers…)</script></html>

cases.title: A real PNG named payload.exe is accepted and recorded as image/png (extension ignored)
cases.steps: POST /api/documents, part filename="payload.exe", Content-Type: application/x-msdownload, body = a real 1x1 PNG
cases.expected: 201 with contentType image/png — the stored type comes from the bytes

cases.title: Plain text named notes.pdf is REJECTED
cases.steps: POST /api/documents, filename="notes.pdf", Content-Type: application/pdf, body = plain text

cases.actual: 400 {"file":"Files of this kind cannot be attached (PDF, PNG, JPEG, Word or Excel only)"}

cases.title: A %PDF- polyglot with an HTML/script body is accepted by the sniffer, and served inert
cases.steps: POST a file beginning "%PDF-1.7" and continuing as HTML with a <script>; then download it
cases.expected: magic-byte sniffing accepts it as a PDF (by design), and the download is attachment + nosniff + CSP default-src 'none' + application/octet-stream so no script can run in the app's origin
cases.actual: upload 201 contentType=application/pdf; download headers: type=application/octet-stream nosniff=nosniff csp=default-src 'none' disposition=attachment; filename="polyglot.pdf"; filename*=UTF-8''polygl
cases.evidence: Sniffing is by magic bytes only (ContentSniffer.detect), so any file whose first 5 bytes are "%PDF-" passes the allow-list whatever follows. AC-C13 is the control that matters here.

cases.title: Filename attack — POSIX traversal: "../../../../etc/passwd"
cases.steps: POST /api/documents with part filename="../../../../etc/passwd"
cases.expected: accepted (201) or refused (400) with a display name that holds no path separator and no control character; never a 5xx and never a dropped connection

cases.title: Filename attack — Windows traversal: "..\\..\\windows\\system32\\cmd.png"
cases.steps: POST /api/documents with part filename="..\\..\\windows\\system32\\cmd.png"
cases.expected: accepted (201) or refused (400) with a display name that holds no path separator and no control character; never a 5xx and never a dropped connection

cases.title: Filename attack — absolute path: "/etc/passwd"
cases.steps: POST /api/documents with part filename="/etc/passwd"
cases.expected: accepted (201) or refused (400) with a display name that holds no path separator and no control character; never a 5xx and never a dropped connection

cases.title: Filename attack — null byte: "shell\u0000.pdf"
cases.steps: POST /api/documents with part filename="shell\u0000.pdf"
cases.expected: accepted (201) or refused (400) with a display name that holds no path separator and no control character; never a 5xx and never a dropped connection
cases.evidence: backend log: org.springframework.web.multipart.MultipartException: Failed to parse multipart servlet request, caused by org.apache.tomcat.util.http.fileupload.InvalidFileNameException — nothing maps it, so GlobalExceptionHandler answers 500 "Unexpected error"
cases.codeRef: backend/src/main/java/com/geneinvoice/document/DocumentUploadAdvice.java:35 (handles MaxUploadSizeExceededException only; no handler for MultipartException)

cases.title: Filename attack — CRLF header injection: "a\r\nX-Injected: yes\r\n.pdf"
cases.steps: POST /api/documents with part filename="a\r\nX-Injected: yes\r\n.pdf"
cases.expected: accepted (201) or refused (400) with a display name that holds no path separator and no control character; never a 5xx and never a dropped connection

cases.title: Filename attack — doubled-up traversal: "....//....//secret.pdf"

cases.title: Filename attack — the parent directory itself: ".."
cases.steps: POST /api/documents with part filename=".."
cases.expected: accepted (201) or refused (400) with a display name that holds no path separator and no control character; never a 5xx and never a dropped connection

cases.title: The server survives every filename attack and keeps serving
cases.steps: After the traversal / null byte / CRLF / over-long attempts, list documents and upload a normal PDF
cases.expected: list 200 and upload 201 — the process is up and the endpoint still works

cases.title: A null byte anywhere in the filename is answered consistently, never with a 5xx
cases.steps: POST /api/documents four times with the null byte leading, in the middle, before the extension, and alone
cases.expected: the same answer whichever position — the app's validation error or a 201 with the byte stripped; never a 500
cases.actual: leading: 201 filename="boot.pdf"; middle: 500 "Unexpected error"; before extension: 500 "Unexpected error"; on its own: 201 filename="file"
cases.evidence: Tomcat's multipart parser throws InvalidFileNameException for a null byte it sees, which reaches no handler; DocumentRules.cleanFilename would have stripped it, but is never called for those requests

cases.title: A CRLF filename cannot inject a response header on download

cases.evidence: PRD AC-C12 says "cannot upload... unless the Open Questions resolve otherwise"; the implementation doc resolves it to yes. Flagged for the reviewer, not scored as a defect.
